title: Evaluating job opportunities using multiple decision signals
text: Hi, I'm Sanjana Alapati. And this video explains how the reallocation engine evaluates job opportunities using multiple decision signals. A job can look promising at first, but one positive factor does not always make it a strong opportunity.

title: Sponsorship history and job liveness checks
text: The reallocation engine looks at several signals together to help students decide where to focus their effort. One signal is sponsorship history. This looks at whether a company has previously sponsored or hired international talent.

title: Resume fit and role quality alignment
text: It can provide useful evidence, but past sponsorship does not guarantee future sponsorship. Another signal is job liveliness. title: OPT timing constraints and weighting signal combinations
text: Considers resume fit and role quality. Resume fit looks at how closely a candidate's skills and experience match the job requirements. title: Grouping opportunities (Apply, Consider, Skip) and preserving human judgment
text: Opportunity may become less useful if the hiring timeline or start date does not work with the student's OPT situation. In some cases, timeline concerns can outweigh otherwise positive signals. These signals work together rather than independently. For example, a role might have strong resume fit, but if the posting is inactive and sponsorship evidence is weak, the overall recommendation may still be lower. Opportunities can then be grouped into apply, consider, or skip. The reallocation engine is designed to support judgment, not replace it. Public data can be incomplete or outdated, and company policies can change. The goal is simple. Use multiple signals to focus your effort on stronger opportunities, while keeping the final decision in your hands.
